Migration = .page { -> .page.standard { in Page.css (5 rules), the word standard added to 7 opted-out call sites, and every --measure: none changed to 100% so min() stays valid and a region measure finally inherits. assign.outcome:
**The grid is already opt-in — in the JS.** `Page.class.js:216` ends every `render()` with `.ac(this.classes ?? 'standard')`, so 137 of 144 in-scope pages already wear `standard` — a word with no CSS rule at all, while the grid sits on a bare unguarded `.page {}` (`Page.css:78`). The owner's sketch is one word away: move `.page {` to `.page.standard {` (5 rules), add `standard` to the 7 call sites that opted out and still want it, and change every `--measure: none` to `100%` so `min()` stays valid and a region's measure finally reaches its pages. Zero `page.js` edits.

**Proved with one headless read** (1440px, `/framework/ext/tabs/`): `.tab-panel` asks for `--measure: none` and the page inside computes `40em` — a 611.19px main track in a 1208px region. `--page-pad: 0` on the same line DID arrive, which is also why `Doc.css:65`'s `.doc-section { --pad-y: 1.5em }` never fires. Also dead: `.page.solo` (0 call sites site-wide).
